title: Production Sync — Dedupe, Retries, Verified Writes, Loud Failures

sections.label: 1 · IT ARRIVES
sections.note: Duplicates and bad payloads are stopped before anything downstream runs.

sections.label: 2 · SHAPE THE DATA
sections.note: Field mapping lives in one place, so a schema change is one edit.

sections.label: 3 · WRITE IT AND CHECK IT LANDED
sections.note: A 200 response is not proof. The record is read back before the run is called a success.

sections.label: 4 · AI ONLY WHERE IT EARNS ITS PLACE
sections.note: One step, doing something a rule could not do.

sections.label: 5 · FAIL LOUDLY
sections.note: Nothing fails quietly. Every run is logged and every failure alerts with a link.

nodes.label: 2 · Have We Already Processed This Event?
nodes.notes: Matched on the event id the sender provides, so a replayed webhook does nothing twice.

nodes.label: 3 · Does the Payload Have Everything We Need?

5 · Map the Fields to What the CRM Expects
6 · Fetch Anything the Payload Left Out
7 · Write the Record to the CRM
nodes.notes: Three attempts with backoff, and the same idempotency key each time so a retry cannot create a second record.

nodes.label: 8 · Read It Back. Did It Actually Land?
9 · Park It for Reprocessing, Do Not Drop It
10 · Write the Account Summary for the CS Team

13 · Alert the Team With a Link to the Run

output_sample.note_on_duplicates: This exact event arrived twice, 40 seconds apart. The second one stopped at step 2.
output_sample.verified: Read back and confirmed. Without this the first timeout would have looked like a failure and been retried into a duplicate.
output_sample.ai_step: Account summary written for the CS team: 42 seats, upgraded from Team, renewal in 71 days, two open tickets both about SSO.
output_sample.if_it_had_failed: Parked in the reprocessing table with the full payload, Slack alert with a link to the execution
